title: Quickfire notes: LLM systems takeaways & experiments (ana f.)
content:
Quickfire capture of ideas and papers I skimmed between Oct 2-8, 2027. Mostly stream-of-consciousness; meant as an inbox for experiments and short hypotheses to hand off to Priya/Owen.

Context: touching the serving runtime and the Optimize tooling next sprint. Focused on: (1) KV cache consistency under model rollouts, (2) batching heuristics for mixed-latency workloads, (3) lightweight evals to detect quality regressions from quant/FP changes.

Top-level takeaways (TL;DR):
- KV cache paper (arXiv 2701.01234) proposes segmented cache invalidation keyed by rollout-version + input-hash. Cheap to implement as metadata stamp on cache entries; allows fast fallback when new variant has shorter context window. Good for Dedicated and Private, avoid cross-customer leakage when model patching.
- Adaptive batching: prefer latency-SLO-aware batching (deadline-based) over fixed-size or fixed-time windows. Workload examples: chatty interactive apps (low tokens per request) benefit from micro-batches with tight deadlines; analytic prompt workloads benefit from larger batching. Suggest experiment: implement deadline-based batching with per-route SLO hints (from Console) and measure P99 token latency + cost.
- Quantization-induced distribution shifts are subtle; need small prompt set evals with calibration metrics (prob vs token, confidence drift). Quick heuristic: per-model token-level KL and next-token perplexity shift on held prompts. If KL > threshold, trigger rollback/fallback to float variant.

Notes on papers / links I liked:
1) "Segmented KV Cache for Versioned Model Serving" (arXiv 2701.01234)
- Idea: attach a short version-tag and compatibility mask to cache entries. Cache lookup computes mask compatibility on the fly; entries with incompatible masks are ignored without full invalidation.
- Pros: low-cost partial invalidation, supports canary rollouts where new variant shares 70% of keys.
- Cons/concerns: mask computation overhead; edge-case when attention params change structurally (mask needs to be conservative).
- Implementation thought: store 1-byte compatibility mask in Redis entry metadata; when model variant registers, compute compatibility bloom quickly via subset tests. For long-term, add heuristics to migrate warm keys instead of recomputing from scratch.

2) "Deadline-aware batching for mixed workloads" (workshop talk, slides linked in Slack)
- Slides show 3 policies: fixed-window, fixed-size, deadline-first. Deadline-first uses per-request deadline derived from desired percentile and current queue depth to decide whether to wait or flush.
- My note: tie this to route-level SLOs from Console. Add token-estimate to decide if joining batch increases expected latency beyond SLO.
- Small simulation I sketched: synthetic mixture of short chat (<40 tokens) and long generations (~512 tokens) at 80/20 ratio. Deadline-first increased throughput 25% while keeping P99 under SLO vs fixed-size which either violated P99 or sacrificed throughput. Need to reproduce on our runtime traces.

3) "Quantization drift detection" (short poster)
- Use small curated evals (50-200 prompts) per model-variant and track multiple signals: next-token KL, token accuracy on golden completions, and semantic similarity (embedding-based) vs float baseline.
- Action framework: if any metric crosses 'soft threshold', mark rollout as degraded but continue low-sampled traffic; if crosses 'hard threshold' -> rollback. This layered approach aligns with Redwood's rollout policies.

Quick experiments to prioritize (rough estimates):
- EXP-1: Implement compatibility-tagged KV entries in our local Redis dev stack. Time: 2 engineer-days + 1 day of test harness. Measure: cache hitrate and invalidation cost during simulated canary. Owner: Owen.
- EXP-2: Deadline-first batching in runtime simulator using existing trace sampler (~1 day to implement simulation). If promising, wire into runtime as opt-in policy behind feature flag. Time: 1 sprint for integration (Priya + infra).
- EXP-3: Build a tiny eval harness (python) that runs 200 prompts through quantized and float variants, computes KL per-token and embedding cosine shifts. Hook to Optimize to auto-suggest "hold rollout" if soft threshold exceeded. Time: 3-4 engineer-days. Owner: me + Priya.

Open questions / unknowns (notes to self):
- How expensive is attaching extra metadata to each KV cache entry at high QPS? Redis overhead might matter: need memory vs CPU tradeoff analysis.
- For deadline batching, how often will backpressure create starvation for large requests? Maybe detect large-request queueing separately and let those preempt smaller ones occasionally.
- Can we subtley reuse existing rollout telemetry (traces/console metrics) to compute compatibility masks automatically? Maybe use model parsing + param fingerprinting to derive masks.

Notes-to-self: micro action items
- Add prototype design doc to Confluence (CONFLUENCE-MLSYS-2027-SUMMARY) with diagrams: cache-tag lifecycle, batch-decision flowchart. (Ana)
- Open a GitHub PR with Redis metadata prototype (link in linked_artifacts). (Owen)
- Run sampling job over last 7 days of Hosted API traces to extract token-length distribution by route. Use that to set default per-route deadline SLO suggestions in Console. (Priya)

Quirky ideas that might be out-of-scope but worth jotting:
- Client-side hinting: expose small optional header where clients can tell runtime "interactive=true" and get preferential small-batch treatment. Risk: misuse by abusive clients; need auth/tiering.
- Warm-key migration: background job that incrementally recomputes compat masks for cached sequences when a new variant stabilizes and then migrates only warm keys to new tag. Could reduce cold bursts on cutover.

Random references / bookmarks to revisit:
- arXiv 2701.01234 (see above)
- Slack thread: #eng-runtime "deadline-batching-experiments" (p02f3a4)
- PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/prs/4821 (prototype kv-tag)

End: keep this doc small and actionable. Will turn these bullets into a short Confluence doc with visuals and handoffs next week.

Notes: keeping version name as "quickfire" so I can search for it. If any of the linked_artifacts move, update the list.

-- Ana
